before.title: 10R80 10-Speed Harsh/Erratic Shifting & Torque Converter Shudder
before.description: The 10R80 transmission paired with the 3.5L EcoBoost suffers axial movement of the CDF clutch drum sleeve, causing internal hydraulic leaks. Owners report harsh 1-2 and 2-3 engagements, clunking on coast-down, shudder at 20-32 mph cruise, and unexpected hard downshifts. Subject of an active class-action lawsuit and multiple Ford TSBs.
before.solution: Have dealer perform the latest TCM/PCM reflash per the current 10R80 harsh-shift TSB (currently 25-2132, superseding 25-2023/24-2046/23-2250) first. If shudder persists, request CDF clutch cylinder and torque-converter repair rather than fluid-only service - generic flushes typically don't resolve it. Document repeated complaints in writing to preserve lemon-law and class-action (O'Connor v. Ford, N.D. Ill.) standing.
symptoms: Delayed engagement from Park or Reverse

proposal.title: 10R80 10-Speed Harsh/Erratic Shifting & Torque Converter Shudder
proposal.description: Ford TSB 25-2476 applies to certain 2018-2021 Lincoln Navigator vehicles with harsh or delayed engagement, harsh or delayed shifting, and sometimes an illuminated MIL with listed transmission DTCs. Ford identifies axial movement of the CDF clutch-cylinder sleeve and resulting hydraulic-circuit leaks as the bulletin condition. The document does not identify torque-converter shudder as a universal Navigator diagnosis, and it does not cover the indexed 2022-2023 years.
proposal.solution: Have a trained transmission technician confirm the vehicle and symptom scope, run the Ford hydraulic circuit leak procedure and inspect the transmission before ordering anything. TSB 25-2476 directs CDF clutch-cylinder replacement only when the test and procedure call for it; additional transmission parts and a cooler flush are only as necessary after inspection. Do not buy a torque converter, valve body, CDF cylinder, fluid or rebuild kit from this page; this is a technician-only diagnosis with no universal retail part.
symptoms: illuminated malfunction indicator with a listed transmission DTC

before.title: 10R80 10-Speed Transmission Harsh/Erratic Shifting & Shudder
before.description: The 10-speed 10R80 automatic in 2018+ Navigators is widely reported to shift harshly, clunk, jerk, hesitate, or shudder between gears. Causes include a sticking torque converter clutch (TCC) regulator valve causing TCC shudder, valve body issues, CDF drum/bushing failure, and control software faults. The problem prompted a class-action lawsuit against Ford over the 10R80.
before.solution: Ford TSBs address the issue with transmission control module/PCM software reflashes, valve body or main control valve body service, and in some cases CDF drum or TCC regulator valve replacement. A transmission fluid service with the correct spec fluid is part of the fix in many cases.
symptoms: Harsh or delayed engagement into gear
Jerking, lunging, or clunking between gears
Shudder or vibration (TCC shudder) at cruising speed

before.title: 3.5L EcoBoost Cam Phaser Rattle (CSP 21N03)
before.description: Internal locking pins in the 3.5L EcoBoost variable cam timing phasers wear out, producing a loud rattle/clack at cold startup and a knocking idle once warm. Ford issued Customer Satisfaction Program 21N03 (and PCM reflash 21B10) replacing all four VCT units, but coverage expired Jan 1, 2023 and out-of-warranty repair runs $2,800-$3,000+.
before.solution: Check VIN at owner.ford.com or lincoln.com/support/recalls for CSP 21N03 eligibility (coverage expired January 1, 2023 — time-limited, not mileage-based). If out of coverage, replace all four VCT phasers, both primary chains, tensioners, guides, and reflash the PCM with the updated 21B10 calibration. Switch to 5,000-mile oil changes with full synthetic 5W-30 to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Diesel-like rattle for 1-3 seconds on cold start

proposal.title: 3.5L EcoBoost Cam Phaser Rattle (CSP 21N03)
proposal.description: Ford Customer Satisfaction Program 21N03 covered certain 2018-2020 Navigator vehicles with the 3.5L GTDI engine after a qualifying 21B10 PCM update. It describes an undesirable cold-start rattle after an extended shut-down or a knocking noise at warm idle from the cam phasers. The one-time program expired January 1, 2023, so this page cannot promise current coverage. The source does not cover model-year 2021.
proposal.solution: Have a Ford or Lincoln technician confirm VIN eligibility, engine, prior calibration and the exact noise. For an affected vehicle that exhibited the covered condition, 21N03 directed replacement of all four VCT units and explicitly said not to replace additional VCT or engine-timing components. Do not buy cam phasers, timing chains, guides, tensioners, an oil kit or other timing parts from this page; current coverage and repair fitment are VIN- and diagnosis-specific.
symptoms: cold-engine start rattle after an extended shutdown

before.title: 3.5L EcoBoost Cam Phaser Rattle / Timing Failure
before.description: Fourth-generation Navigators with the twin-turbo 3.5L EcoBoost V6 commonly develop a loud rattle or diesel-like clacking from the front of the engine, most noticeable for 2-5 seconds on cold startup. The internal locking pin inside the variable camshaft timing (VCT) phasers fails, allowing oil to drain and slack to develop in the timing chain. Left unaddressed it can advance to crank/cam correlation faults and timing damage.
before.solution: Ford issued TSB 20-2315 and Customer Satisfaction Program 21N03 (extended warranty to Jan 1, 2023) covering replacement of all four VCT phasers plus a PCM reflash on 2018-2020 models. Out of warranty, repair involves replacing all four phasers, the primary chain, tensioners, and guides.
symptoms: Loud rattle/clatter from front of engine on cold start

before.title: Navigator 3.5L EcoBoost Timing Chain Stretch
before.description: The 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 in 2015+ Navigator (and shared F-150, Expedition, Edge ST) suffers timing chain stretch typically between 80,000-150,000 miles. Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start, particularly on the passenger-side bank, plus P0016/P0017/P0018/P0019 correlation codes. Causes include extended oil change intervals, low-quality oil, and turbocharger-related oil shear.
before.solution: Full timing chain kit replacement (primary chain, both secondary chains, tensioners, guides, sprockets, water pump) — typically $2,500-$4,500 at dealer, $1,800-$3,000 at independent. Stick to 5,000-7,500 mile oil intervals with Motorcraft full-synthetic 5W-30. Catastrophic chain failure means head rebuild ($6,000+).

proposal.title: Navigator 3.5L EcoBoost Timing Chain Stretch
proposal.description: The exact Ford communication found for the indexed years is SSM 49821, which lists 2015-2021 Navigator vehicles and VCT DTCs P0011, P0012, P0014, P0015, P0016, P0017, P0018, P0019, P0021, P0022, P0024 and P0025. Ford says those codes may result from debris causing a VCT solenoid to stick and requires a pinpoint-test cycling step before replacement. That source does not establish a model-wide timing-chain-stretch condition, failure rate, mileage threshold or automatic engine damage.
proposal.solution: Have a technician reproduce any noise, scan all modules and follow Ford pinpoint testing. When an applicable VCT code is present, SSM 49821 says to cycle the affected VCT solenoid ten times to attempt to clear debris before replacing the solenoid. Do not buy a timing-chain kit, guides, tensioners, phasers, water pump or engine from this page; the listed codes do not prove timing-chain stretch and the correct repair depends on diagnosis.
symptoms: malfunction indicator with an applicable VCT DTC
engine noise requiring diagnosis rather than assumed chain stretch

before.title: 5.4L 3-Valve Triton Spark Plugs Seize and Break in Cylinder Head
before.description: Second- and third-generation Navigators with the 5.4L 3-valve Triton V8 use a unique two-piece spark plug whose long electrode shell extends below the threads. Carbon deposits cake into the gap over high mileage, gripping the plug so tightly that the shell breaks off during removal, leaving a portion seized inside the aluminum cylinder head. This turns a routine tune-up into a costly extraction job.
before.solution: Ford released special extraction tool kits and a procedure: remove plugs only on a cold engine using hand tools, soak with penetrating oil, and break carbon loose gradually. Many owners preemptively replace plugs by ~60k-80k miles to reduce the risk. Broken plugs require an extractor (and sometimes head removal if a fragment falls in).
symptoms: Difficulty removing spark plugs during service
Plug breaks off / shell stuck in head
Misfire if attempted DIY goes wrong
Rough running / check engine light from misfire

proposal.title: 5.4L 3-Valve Triton Spark Plugs Seize and Break in Cylinder Head
proposal.description: Ford TSB 08-7-6 applies to 2005-2008 Navigator vehicles with a 5.4L 3-valve engine built before October 9, 2007. It documents difficult spark-plug removal that can damage or separate a two-piece plug and leave part of it in the cylinder head. The bulletin does not support the indexed 2004 year on one preserved page.
proposal.solution: This bulletin is written for trained professionals and requires the engine to be at room temperature; removing plugs from a warm or hot engine increases thread-damage risk. Its procedure calls for a limited initial turn, Motorcraft Carburetor Tune-Up Cleaner, at least a 15-minute soak and hand tools, with Ford special tools for specific breakage modes. Do not buy aftermarket extractors, replacement plugs, penetrating oil, cleaner or anti-seize from this page; have a qualified technician follow the current Ford procedure and verify the engine build date.
symptoms: part of the spark plug remains in the cylinder head

before.title: 5.4L 3V Triton Two-Piece Spark Plug Breaks on Removal
before.description: Factory Motorcraft PZT-2FE two-piece platinum plugs in the 5.4L 3V Triton seize in the head from carbon buildup around the ground-electrode shield. Attempting normal removal cracks the plug, leaving the lower shell stuck in the cylinder head and requiring specialized extractor kits or head removal to recover.
before.solution: Soak each plug with penetrating oil (PB Blaster or Seafoam Deep Creep) with engine warm but not hot. Back out 1/8 to 1/4 turn, re-soak, work back and forth before full removal. Use OTC 6918 Triton 3V extractor kit if a plug breaks. Replace with one-piece Champion 7989 or Motorcraft SP-546 (later redesign); apply nickel anti-seize to the smooth lower electrode shell (NOT the threads, per Motorcraft) and torque to 25 ft-lbs.
symptoms: Lower electrode shell stuck in head

before.title: Navigator 5.4L 3V Triton Spark Plug Breakage on Removal
before.description: The 5.4L 3-valve Triton V8 in 2005-2008 Navigator (and shared F-150/Expedition) uses a two-piece spark plug (Motorcraft SP-515/SP-546) that frequently snaps off in the cylinder head during removal. The lower portion stays welded into the head by carbon, leaving the upper electrode in the socket. Common at 60,000-100,000 miles when the first plug change is attempted.

Use the Lisle 65600 / OTC 6918 broken-plug extraction kit if breakage occurs (~$80). Replace with the redesigned one-piece Motorcraft SP-546 / NGK plugs. Ford settled a class-action covering reasonable extraction costs at dealer.

before.title: Air Ride Suspension Compressor Burnout from Air Bag Leaks
before.description: The air suspension's rubber air springs develop pinhole leaks at the upper crimp ring after 8-12 years. 4WD models use a 4-corner system; 2WD models use rear-only. The OEM Continental/AMK compressor (mounted with integrated dryer) runs continuously trying to maintain ride height, eventually burning out. Owners wake to a vehicle sitting on the bump stops and a compressor that hums but no longer builds pressure. NOTE: 4th-generation Navigator (2018+) replaced air suspension with coil-spring adaptive damping and is NOT affected.
before.solution: Diagnose with soapy water at each air spring upper crimp before replacing the compressor. Replace leaking bags in pairs (front or rear) with Arnott/Suncore units and install a new compressor (Arnott P-2932 for 97-06, P-2937/U326 for 07-13) with dryer. For owners who don't tow, Strutmasters/Arnott coil-conversion kits eliminate the problem permanently for $400-700.
symptoms: Vehicle sagging or sitting on rear bump stops in the morning
Compressor runs continuously or won't shut off
Compressor hums but ride height won't rise
Air ride fault message on dash

proposal.title: Air Ride Suspension Compressor Burnout from Air Bag Leaks
proposal.description: NHTSA complaint ODI 10025237 reports a 1999 Navigator air-suspension compressor failure, and ODI 10360339 reports a 2003 vehicle whose air-suspension motor was replaced and whose air bags allegedly leaked and filled slowly in cold weather. These are individual owner allegations with no reported injuries or deaths, not proof of a universal leak mechanism, compressor-burnout sequence, incidence rate or coverage across every indexed year.
proposal.solution: If the vehicle sags, rides unevenly or the compressor runs excessively, have the complete air-suspension system diagnosed for stored faults, power and ground, height-sensor input, lines, fittings, springs and compressor performance. Do not buy an air spring, compressor, dryer, relay, conversion kit or named aftermarket brand from this page; configuration and failed component must be confirmed on the vehicle.
symptoms: vehicle sag or uneven ride height
slow height recovery in cold weather
air-suspension compressor inoperative or running excessively

before.title: Navigator Rear Air Suspension Bag/Compressor Failure
before.description: 2003-2017 Navigators with the optional/standard rear air suspension (and the 2003+ Expedition with the same system) develop air-bag leaks at the bag-to-piston seal as the bag rubber ages and cracks. Symptoms: rear of vehicle sagging overnight, compressor running constantly, error message "Check Air Suspension." Eventually the compressor burns out from constant duty.
before.solution: Replace air bags as a pair (Arnott or Strutmasters aftermarket ~$400-$700 per side; OEM Motorcraft ~$800-$1,200 per side installed). Replace the dryer with the compressor or it will quickly fail again. Some owners convert to coil springs (Strutmasters kit ~$700) — eliminates the leveling feature but is permanent.

proposal.title: Brake Master Cylinder Internal Leak (Recall 25S37)
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 25V236/Ford 25S37 covers certain 2017-2018 Navigator vehicles. The brake master cylinder may allow brake fluid to leak from the front-wheel circuit into the brake booster, reducing brake function and increasing stopping distance. Applicability is VIN-specific; the indexed years alone do not establish that a vehicle is recalled.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for open recall 25S37/25V236. Dealers will replace the brake master cylinder and, if the master cylinder is leaking, also replace the brake booster, free of charge. If brake function is reduced or stopping distance changes, stop driving when safe and arrange service or towing. Do not buy a master cylinder, booster or brake-fluid kit from this page; this is a VIN-scoped dealer recall remedy.
symptoms: brake fluid leaking from the front-wheel circuit into the booster

before.title: Deployable Power Running Board Motor Failure & Linkage Corrosion
before.description: The Dorman-supplied power running board motors and pivot/swivel brackets on 2007-2014 (3rd-gen) and 2015-2017 (3rd-gen refresh) Navigators corrode and seize from road salt and water exposure, especially in northern states. Boards stop deploying, hang in mid-position, or cycle repeatedly. Brackets with dissimilar-metal mounting can crack and drop the board. On 2018+ (4th-gen) trucks the failures are more often electrical/settings-related (boards switching from AUTO to OFF, one-side-only operation) rather than pure mechanical corrosion.
before.solution: Pull the affected board, free the linkage with PB Blaster, lube all pivots with marine grease. If motor is dead, OE replacement (Ford 9L7Z-16A507-A family) is ~$500/side, aftermarket Dorman motor+bracket assemblies run $150-300. On 2018+ trucks, first verify board mode is set to AUTO and check battery health before replacing hardware. Scan the BCM for B-codes to confirm which side before ordering.
symptoms: Running board stuck open or closed
Board cycles in/out repeatedly while driving
One side works, the other doesn't

proposal.title: Deployable Power Running Board Motor Failure & Linkage Corrosion
proposal.description: Ford SSM 50154 covers 2018-2020 Navigator running boards disabled after a low-battery event, with the setting moved from Auto to Off and possible DTC U3003:16. SSM 51737 covers some 2022-2023 vehicles whose setting defaults to Off after a key cycle and says the condition does not affect durability. A separate 2006 owner complaint alleges support-post corrosion, but it does not prove a universal motor or linkage defect across the indexed 2007-2024 range.
proposal.solution: For a 2018-2020 disabled-board condition, inspect the charging system, correct the low-voltage event and restore Auto mode as SSM 50154 directs. For the 2022-2023 setting condition, Ford said no service was recommended at publication and owners could temporarily reset Auto mode. Physical sticking, looseness or corrosion needs hands-on inspection. Do not buy a motor, linkage, hinge, control module or lubricant from this page; the correct path depends on year, fault and mechanical condition.
symptoms: running boards disabled or setting changed to Off
setting defaults to Off after a key cycle
physical sticking or looseness requiring inspection

before.title: Deployable Power Running Boards Stick / Fail to Retract
before.description: Navigators equipped with deployable (power) running boards commonly have boards that stick in the deployed or retracted position, deploy on only one side, or retract and then immediately redeploy. Failures stem from corroded/seized motors (original Dorman-type units on 2007-2014 models) and dirt or ice binding the swivel arm linkage. The board assembly is sold as a complete unit, making repairs expensive.
before.solution: Clean and lubricate the pivot joints/arms (white lithium grease) for binding; replace the running board motor or the entire board assembly when the motor or swivel brackets fail. Some owners disable the feature to avoid winter ice hazards.
symptoms: Running board won't retract or won't deploy

proposal.title: Deployable Power Running Boards Stick / Fail to Retract
proposal.description: Ford SSM 50154 documents disabled running boards on certain 2018-2020 Navigator vehicles after a low-battery event, sometimes with DTC U3003:16. A board that physically sticks or cannot support weight needs mechanical inspection before use. before.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure (Clicking, Wrong Temperature)
before.description: Second- and third-generation Navigators commonly suffer failed HVAC blend door actuators. The small electric motor that positions the temperature/mode doors strips its internal gears, producing a repetitive clicking or 'whir-click' noise from behind the dash or rear panel and causing one zone to blow the wrong temperature (e.g., rear blows warm while front blows cold). In some cases the blend door itself binds.
before.solution: Replace the failed blend door actuator(s); the rear unit is reached behind the right rear panel and front units behind the dash/radio. If clicking persists after replacement, the blend door linkage may be stuck and needs freeing or repair.
symptoms: Repetitive clicking or knocking behind dash or rear trim
One zone blows wrong temperature (warm instead of cold or vice versa)
Temperature won't change with control setting

proposal.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure (Clicking, Wrong Temperature)
proposal.description: A review of 1,314 Navigator manufacturer-communication records did not identify an exact bulletin establishing a model-wide 2003-2014 blend-door-actuator failure, a universal clicking mechanism or an incidence rate. The indexed identity is retained, but the present evidence does not justify diagnosing every wrong-temperature or clicking complaint as an actuator.
proposal.solution: Have the HVAC system diagnosed for actuator command and feedback, door movement, control inputs, refrigerant performance, heater-core flow and wiring before replacing anything. Do not buy a blend-door actuator, HVAC control module or door assembly from this page; there is no verified universal retail part or model-wide manufacturer repair for this indexed claim.

temperature or mode door not responding correctly

before.title: Power Liftgate Opens / Operates on Its Own
before.description: Fourth-gen Navigator owners frequently report the hands-free power liftgate opening or cycling by itself, sometimes while parked or triggered by opening a driver door or even nearby beeping sounds. The root cause is typically a faulty liftgate release switch, hands-free kick sensor, or wiring harness, compounded by software glitches in the body control module.
before.solution: TSB 18-2089 addresses early 2018 units with a liftgate release switch and wiring harness replacement. Owners report success replacing the tailgate/hands-free sensor and applying dealer software updates; a battery reset sometimes clears intermittent glitches before hardware replacement.
symptoms: Liftgate reopens immediately after being closed
Liftgate triggered by door operation or external sounds

proposal.title: Power Liftgate Opens / Operates on Its Own
proposal.description: NHTSA complaint ODI 11187451 alleges that one stationary 2018 Navigator’s liftgate opened unexpectedly, with no injury or death reported. Ford SSM 49914 covers a different condition—an inoperative power liftgate on 2018-2021 Navigator vehicles caused by rear-gate trunk-module software. That SSM does not establish the cause of uncommanded opening, and one complaint does not prove a common sensor, latch, motor or module failure.
proposal.solution: If the liftgate moves without a command, keep people clear, disable hands-free operation if the owner manual permits and arrange diagnosis of keys, switches, sensors, latch state, wiring and module data. Use SSM 49914 only when the liftgate is inoperative and its criteria are met; it directs RGTM reprogramming. Do not buy a kick sensor, latch, strut, motor or module from this page because the uncommanded condition has no verified universal part or remedy.
symptoms: liftgate allegedly opens without an intended command
power liftgate inoperative on an applicable 2018-2021 vehicle

before.title: SYNC 3 / SYNC 4 Infotainment Freezing, Black Screen, and Touch Unresponsiveness
before.description: The SYNC 3 (2018-2020) and SYNC 4 (2021+) head unit in the 4th-generation Navigator freezes, reboots mid-drive, displays a black screen with spinning loader, loses touch response, drops Bluetooth pairing, or fails to show the backup camera. Issue is typically an APIM (Accessory Protocol Interface Module) firmware bug or hardware fault. Note: The 2015 Navigator (final year of 3rd-gen) is the only Navigator that ever shipped with MyLincoln Touch / SYNC 2; 2010-2014 Navigators ran SYNC 1, a different system not affected by the MyFord/MyLincoln Touch class action.
before.solution: Soft reset: hold power + seek-right ~10 seconds until reboot. If that fails, perform a master reset (Settings > General > Master Reset) and install the latest SYNC update from owner.lincoln.com via USB. For persistent failure, disconnect the negative battery cable for 10 minutes. Dealer APIM replacement runs $800-1500 if the module is dead. The MyFord/MyLincoln Touch class settlement (Case 3:13-cv-03072) only covered Ford/Lincoln vehicles purchased before August 9, 2013, and the claim period has closed — Navigator owners are not eligible since the Navigator did not receive MyLincoln Touch until MY2015.
symptoms: Bluetooth/phone won't pair or drops calls

proposal.title: SYNC 3 / SYNC 4 Infotainment Freezing, Black Screen, and Touch Unresponsiveness
proposal.description: Ford TSB 21-2411 covers certain 2020-2021 Navigator vehicles with SYNC 3 concerns including a frozen or blank touchscreen, connection and audio problems, and other software symptoms. Ford TSB 25-2055 covers 2022-2024 Navigator vehicles with general stability, intermittent reboot, wireless CarPlay or Android Auto, phone-audio, navigation/GPS and Alexa concerns. These sources do not cover every indexed 2018-2019 vehicle and do not establish a blanket APIM hardware failure.
proposal.solution: Confirm the SYNC generation, vehicle year, current software and exact symptom. TSB 21-2411 directs a SYNC 3 APIM software update for qualifying vehicles; TSB 25-2055 requires checking recent OTA history and available GWM, APIM and TCU updates before following its technician procedure. Do not buy an APIM, display, USB hub or replacement radio from this page; update eligibility and any later hardware diagnosis are vehicle-specific.
symptoms: CarPlay, Android Auto, audio or navigation instability
